 URBN Reports Record Q3 Sales and Profits 
 PHILADELPHIA, PA, November 24, 2026 – Urban Outfitters, Inc. (NASDAQ:URBN), a leading lifestyle products and services company which operates a portfolio of global consumer brands including the Anthropologie, Free People, FP Movement, Urban Outfitters and Nuuly brands, today announced net income of $134.1 million and earnings per diluted share of $1.54 for the three months ended October 31, 2026. For the nine months ended October 31, 2026, net income was $490.4 million and earnings per diluted share were $5.61. 
 For the nine months ended October 31, 2026, adjusted net income was $399.3 million and adjusted earnings per diluted share were $4.57. Adjusted net income and adjusted earnings per diluted share for the nine months ended October 31, 2026, exclude one-time benefits related to refunds for tariffs previously paid under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act ("IEEPA"), associated interest income and a tax benefit related to the release of a valuation allowance against certain foreign net deferred tax assets. See “Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Financial Measures” included at the end of this release. 
 Total Company net sales for the three months ended October 31, 2026, increased 8.9% to a record $1.67 billion. Total Retail segment net sales increased 6.1%, with comparable Retail segment net sales increasing 4.4%. The increase in Retail segment comparable net sales was driven by mid single-digit positive growth in both retail store sales and digital channel sales. Comparable Retail segment net sales increased 8.5% at FP Group, 5.8% at Urban Outfitters and 1.7% at Anthropologie Group. Subscription segment net sales increased 28.0% primarily driven by a 27.6% increase in average active subscribers in the current quarter versus the prior year quarter. Wholesale segment net sales increased 18.8% driven by a 20.8% increase in FP Group wholesale sales primarily due to an increase in sales to specialty customers and department stores. 
 For the nine months ended October 31, 2026, total Company net sales increased 10.2% to a record $4.81 billion. Total Retail segment net sales increased 7.3%, with comparable Retail segment net sales increasing 5.4%. The increase in Retail segment comparable net sales was driven by mid single-digit positive growth in both digital channel sales and retail store sales. Comparable Retail segment net sales increased 9.4% at FP Group, 7.8% at Urban Outfitters and 2.2% at Anthropologie Group. Subscription segment net sales increased 30.2% primarily driven by a 30.3% increase in average active subscribers in the current period versus the prior year period. Wholesale segment net sales increased 20.6% driven by a 22.0% increase in FP Group wholesale sales primarily due to an increase in sales to specialty customers and department stores. 
 “Our teams delivered another standout quarter, achieving record third-quarter sales and earnings per share,” said Richard A. Hayne, Chief Executive Officer. “Every brand and segment contributed positively to our third-quarter performance, underscoring the strength of our portfolio and disciplined execution across the organization,” finished Mr. Hayne.

 4,363,606 | For the three months ended October 31, 2026, the gross profit rate increased by 26 basis points compared to the three months ended October 31, 2025, and gross profit dollars increased 9.6% to $617.6 million from $563.3 million. The increase in gross profit rate was primarily driven by leverage in initial merchandise costs due in part to the lower year over year impact of tariffs which was partially offset by higher inbound freight fuel surcharges, leverage in delivery expense as a result of several company initiatives, and leverage in store occupancy costs due to the increase in total Company net sales. These benefits were partially offset by an increase in Retail segment markdowns primarily driven by Anthropologie Group. The increase in gross profit dollars was primarily due to higher net sales. 
 For the nine months ended October 31, 2026, the gross profit rate increased by 204 basis points compared to the nine months ended October 31, 2025, and gross profit dollars increased 16.3% to $1.88 billion from $1.62 billion. For the nine months ended October 31, 2026, the adjusted gross profit rate increased by 5 basis points compared to the nine months ended October 31, 2025, and adjusted gross profit dollars increased 10.3% to $1.79 billion from $1.62 billion. The increase in the adjusted gross profit rate was primarily driven by leverage in delivery expense as a result of several company initiatives and leverage in store occupancy costs due to the increase in total Company net sales, partially offset by an increase in Retail segment markdowns primarily driven by Anthropologie Group. The increase in adjusted gross profit dollars was primarily due to higher net sales. 
 As of October 31, 2026, total inventory increased by $84.4 million, or 10.1%, compared to total inventory as of October 31, 2025. Total Retail segment inventory increased 9.2% and Retail segment comparable inventory increased 5.6%. Wholesale segment inventory increased 21.6%. The increase in inventory for both segments was due to the increase in net sales and timing of inventory receipts. 
 For the three months ended October 31, 2026, selling, general and administrative expenses increased by $26.5 million, or 6.3%, compared to the three months ended October 31, 2025. Selling, general and administrative expenses leveraged 64 basis points as a percentage of net sales compared to the three months ended October 31, 2025. The leverage in selling, general and administrative expenses as a percentage of net sales for the three months ended October 31, 2026, as compared to the prior year quarter was primarily from leverage in store payroll expenses due to the growth in Retail segment store net sales and lower incentive-based compensation costs. The dollar growth in selling, general and administrative expenses was primarily due to higher marketing expenses to support customer and net sales growth in the Retail and Subscription segments, as well as increased store payroll expenses to support the growth in Retail segment store net sales. 
 For the nine months ended October 31, 2026, selling, general and administrative expenses increased by $109.6 million, or 9.4%, compared to the nine months ended October 31, 2025. Selling, general and administrative expenses leveraged 21 basis points as a percentage of net sales compared to the nine months ended October 31, 2025. The leverage in selling, general and administrative expenses as a percentage of net sales for the nine months ended October 31, 2026, as compared to the prior year period was primarily from leverage in store payroll expenses due to the growth in Retail segment store net sales, lower incentive-based compensation costs, and a discrete benefit of $6.9 million, or 14 basis points, in the current year period due to 
 the reversal of a litigation accrual. These benefits were partially offset by deleverage in marketing expenses to support customer and net sales growth in the Retail and Subscription segments. The dollar growth in selling, general and administrative expenses was primarily due to higher marketing expenses to support customer and net sales growth in the Retail and Subscription segments, as well as increased store payroll expenses to support the growth in Retail segment store net sales. 
 The Company’s effective tax rate for the three months ended October 31, 2026, was 24.8%, compared to 23.6% in the three months ended October 31, 2025. The Company's effective tax rate for the nine months ended October 31, 2026, was 21.3%, compared to 22.2% in the nine months ended October 31, 2025. The Company's adjusted effective tax rate for the nine months ended October 31, 2026, was 23.6%. The increase in the effective tax rate for the three months ended October 31, 2026, and the increase in the adjusted effective tax rate for the nine months ended October 31, 2026, was primarily attributable to the ratio of foreign taxable earnings to global taxable earnings. 
 Net income for the three months ended October 31, 2026, was $134.1 million and earnings per diluted share were $1.54. Net income for the nine months ended October 31, 2026, was $490.4 million and earnings per diluted share were $5.61. Adjusted net income for the nine months ended October 31, 2026, was $399.3 million and adjusted earnings per diluted share were $4.57. 
 On June 4, 2019, the Company’s Board of Directors authorized the repurchase of 20 million common shares under a share repurchase program. During the nine months ended October 31, 2026, the Company repurchased and subsequently retired 4.6 million shares for approximately $300 million. During the year ended January 31, 2026, the Company repurchased and subsequently retired 3.3 million shares for approximately $154 million. As of October 31, 2026, 10.0 million common shares were remaining under the program.

 Urban Outfitters, Inc. offers lifestyle-oriented general merchandise and consumer products and services through a portfolio of global consumer brands. The Company operates omni-channel retail operations including stores, websites and catalogs for the Anthropologie, Free People, FP Movement and Urban Outfitters brands across the United States, Canada and Europe; Menus & Venues restaurants; and Urban Outfitters and Anthropologie Group franchisee-owned stores in the Middle East. Free People, FP Movement and Urban Outfitters wholesale sell products to department and specialty stores worldwide, digital businesses and the Company's Retail segment. Nuuly is primarily a women's apparel subscription rental service offering a wide selection of rental product from the Company's own brands, third-party brands and one-of-a-kind vintage pieces.

The increase in gross profit rate was primarily driven by leverage in initial merchandise costs due in part to the lower year over year impact of tariffs which was partially offset by higher inbound freight fuel surcharges, leverage in delivery expense as a result of several company initiatives, and leverage in store occupancy costs due to the increase in total Company net sales. These benefits were partially offset by an increase in Retail segment markdowns primarily driven by Anthropologie Group. The increase in gross profit dollars was primarily due to higher net sales. 
 For the nine months ended October 31, 2026, the gross profit rate increased by 204 basis points compared to the nine months ended October 31, 2025, and gross profit dollars increased 16.3% to $1.88 billion from $1.62 billion. For the nine months ended October 31, 2026, the adjusted gross profit rate increased by 5 basis points compared to the nine months ended October 31, 2025, and adjusted gross profit dollars increased 10.3% to $1.79 billion from $1.62 billion. The increase in the adjusted gross profit rate was primarily driven by leverage in delivery expense as a result of several company initiatives and leverage in store occupancy costs due to the increase in total Company net sales, partially offset by an increase in Retail segment markdowns primarily driven by Anthropologie Group. The increase in adjusted gross profit dollars was primarily due to higher net sales. 
 As of October 31, 2026, total inventory increased by $84.4 million, or 10.1%, compared to total inventory as of October 31, 2025. Total Retail segment inventory increased 9.2% and Retail segment comparable inventory increased 5.6%. Wholesale segment inventory increased 21.6%. The increase in inventory for both segments was due to the increase in net sales and timing of inventory receipts. 
 For the three months ended October 31, 2026, selling, general and administrative expenses increased by $26.5 million, or 6.3%, compared to the three months ended October 31, 2025. Selling, general and administrative expenses leveraged 64 basis points as a percentage of net sales compared to the three months ended October 31, 2025. The leverage in selling, general and administrative expenses as a percentage of net sales for the three months ended October 31, 2026, as compared to the prior year quarter was primarily from leverage in store payroll expenses due to the growth in Retail segment store net sales and lower incentive-based compensation costs. The dollar growth in selling, general and administrative expenses was primarily due to higher marketing expenses to support customer and net sales growth in the Retail and Subscription segments, as well as increased store payroll expenses to support the growth in Retail segment store net sales. 
 For the nine months ended October 31, 2026, selling, general and administrative expenses increased by $109.6 million, or 9.4%, compared to the nine months ended October 31, 2025. Selling, general and administrative expenses leveraged 21 basis points as a percentage of net sales compared to the nine months ended October 31, 2025. The leverage in selling, general and administrative expenses as a percentage of net sales for the nine months ended October 31, 2026, as compared to the prior year period was primarily from leverage in store payroll expenses due to the growth in Retail segment store net sales, lower incentive-based compensation costs, and a discrete benefit of $6.9 million, or 14 basis points, in the current year period due to 
 the reversal of a litigation accrual. These benefits were partially offset by deleverage in marketing expenses to support customer and net sales growth in the Retail and Subscription segments. The dollar growth in selling, general and administrative expenses was primarily due to higher marketing expenses to support customer and net sales growth in the Retail and Subscription segments, as well as increased store payroll expenses to support the growth in Retail segment store net sales. 
 The Company’s effective tax rate for the three months ended October 31, 2026, was 24.8%, compared to 23.6% in the three months ended October 31, 2025. The Company's effective tax rate for the nine months ended October 31, 2026, was 21.3%, compared to 22.2% in the nine months ended October 31, 2025. The Company's adjusted effective tax rate for the nine months ended October 31, 2026, was 23.6%. The increase in the effective tax rate for the three months ended October 31, 2026, and the increase in the adjusted effective tax rate for the nine months ended October 31, 2026, was primarily attributable to the ratio of foreign taxable earnings to global taxable earnings.

 Urban Outfitters, Inc. offers lifestyle-oriented general merchandise and consumer products and services through a portfolio of global consumer brands. The Company operates omni-channel retail operations including stores, websites and catalogs for the Anthropologie, Free People, FP Movement and Urban Outfitters brands across the United States, Canada and Europe; Menus & Venues restaurants; and Urban Outfitters and Anthropologie Group franchisee-owned stores in the Middle East. Free People, FP Movement and Urban Outfitters wholesale sell products to department and specialty stores worldwide, digital businesses and the Company's Retail segment. Nuuly is primarily a women's apparel subscription rental service offering a wide selection of rental product from the Company's own brands, third-party brands and one-of-a-kind vintage pieces.
